newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dexia, Groupe San Paolo in long-term pact.
newsitem.headline: Dexia, Groupe San Paolo in long-term pact.

text.p: Franco-Belgian bank Dexia said on Monday it had agreed a long-term strategic co-operation pact with Italy's group San Paolo and would take a 40 percent stake in Italy's Crediop.
In a statement, Dexia said the price would be between 1.6 and 1.9 billion French francs, the final price depending on the Crediop performance in the next three years.
Dexia said it also planned to take a one percent stake in Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino during its privatisation later in 1997.
Dexia was created in October out of the merger of Credit Local de France and Credit Communal de Belgique.
The operation will be financed by Dexia's own funds and will be positive for the results and profitability from 1997, Dexia said in the statement.
"Already active in Great Britain, Germany, Spain, Austria and Sweden, Dexia could not be absent from one of the large European Union markets, Italy," Dexia chairman Pierre Richard said.
"By this important operation, Dexia completes its European network," he said.

Dexia said Crediop SpA has a balance sheet total of 110 billion francs ($75.4 billion) and shareholders assets of 3.3 billion francs, making it the biggest local sector bank after Cassa Depositi e Presititi.
Crediop said on Monday it posted an 11-month profit of 71.5 billion lira. It has been under San Paolo ownership since February 1, 1996.
Dexia has a balance sheet total of over 1,000 billion francs and shareholders funds of 40 billion francs.
"This operation demonstrates the new dynamism created by the constitution of the Dexia group whose aim is to improve shareholder value," Richard added.
Istituto Bancario San Paolo's chairman Gianni Zandano said the deal signified a step into one of the most important banking networks in Europe.

He said in a statement that with this move "Crediop and the whole San Paolo group enters into the most important European banking network specialising in financing local authorities and public works."
He said the deal with the Franco-Belgian banking group gave the Turin-based bank considerable possibilities of developing important synergies in Italian and international markets.

"This new relationship of cooperation significantly broadens the network of San Paolo's international strategic alliances and is an important step in preparing the bank for the challenges of a single market and of European monetary union," Zandano said.
CLF-Dexia France shares closed 4.92 percent higher at 533 francs in Paris while the blue-chip index was up 0.2 percent. In Brussels, Dexia was up 125 Belgian francs, or 3.71 percent, at 3,495.
In Milan, San Paolo shares closed 393 lira higher at 11,842. ($ = 1.458 Swiss Francs)
